findings.ac: AC2 demoable end-to-end: watcher flags gemini-3.5-flash silent reroute and gemini-3.1-flash-lite shutdown notice
findings.text: The watcher only classifies models in MODEL_GRADES (grades.js: gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.8-flash x2); neither gemini-3.5-flash nor gemini-3.1-flash-lite is an active grade, so a CLI run with the fixture never flags either event in the report. The tests call classifyModelStatus directly on those names. The CLI test asserts only 'gemini-3.6-flash' (a grade model, status OK) and 'type: research', so no end-to-end assertion shows the two events appear in the generated report.

findings.ac: AC4 Stress: network failure / markup change fail safely with non-zero exit code and error log
findings.text: The only CLI failure test ('fails loud with non-zero exit code (1) and logs to stderr') asserts just .toThrow(); it never checks status === 1, stderr, or the '[FATAL] Model Deprecation Watcher failed' text. Network failure (fetchDeprecationsHtml: !res.ok HTTP error, 15s AbortController timeout) has no test at all; the fixture path bypasses fetch entirely.

findings.ac: AC4 Stress: without corrupting existing reports
findings.text: No test writes a report, then runs a failing run (corrupt fixture or fetch error, non-dry-run) and asserts the prior report is byte-identical. The corrupt-fixture test uses --dry-run, which never reaches writeFileSync; the report write is non-atomic. The no-corruption guarantee rests only on parse running before the write, and no assertion covers it.

findings.ac: AC3 Time-to-Value: report written under docs/research/model-lifecycle/ with clear SIMPLE SWAP / RE-BENCHMARK recommendations
findings.text: No test runs non-dry-run or --out and asserts a file lands in docs/research/model-lifecycle/ with the YYYY-MM-model-deprecation-report.md name (the issue also cites YYYY-MM-DD-deprecation-report.md in the Mental Model; the code uses YYYY-MM). The markdown test classifies the active grades, which are all OK, so the 'Recommended Actions' branch ('[SIMPLE SWAP] Grade ...' / '[RE-BENCHMARK] Grade ...' lines) is never exercised and nothing asserts those strings.

findings.ac: AC1 Verification: --dry-run runs cleanly and generates a validated report
findings.text: Dry-run is only tested with --fixture (which also lowers the sanity floor to 5), never the live-fetch path the AC's literal command uses. 'Validated' is only substring checks (type: research, title, table header); there is no OKF or frontmatter validation. The grade-name assertions toContain('light'/'medium'/'high'/'extreme') are weak and would pass on incidental text.

Only the '--check exits 0 when all OK' direction is tested, and it asserts only expect(stdout).toBeDefined(). No test shows --check exits 1 when a grade has a SILENT REROUTE or SHUTDOWN status, though the workflow's alert step depends on it. The workflow also cannot tell a fetch/parse failure (exit 1) from a deprecation (exit 1), so network failures would open a misleading deprecation advisory issue.

findings.ac: Path: ACCESS RESTRICTED classification and token pricing deltas
findings.text: The ACCESS RESTRICTED branch (legacy gemini-1.* / gemini-2.0* prefix heuristic in classifyModelStatus) has no test. The issue's 'Calculate token pricing deltas where published' has no implementation or test (grep shows no pricing code).
